georgia-first-days.title: Our first days in Georgia: arriving at night and exploring Tbilisi
georgia-first-days.description: The start of our 17-day trip with Anya: why sleep matters after a night flight and what we remember about Tbilisi’s botanical garden.
georgia-first-days.label: Georgia / The journey begins
georgia-first-days.alt: Vlad on a bridge in Tbilisi’s botanical garden
georgia-first-days.cardTitle: Georgia. The first days of a big adventure
georgia-first-days.cardDescription: A night flight, old Tbilisi and a walk worth getting some sleep for.
georgia-first-days.body:
Our first big trip together. Seventeen days in Georgia, our suitcases and Anya beside me. The plan included Tbilisi, Kazbegi, Kakheti and Batumi. But first came a night on a plane and several hours to wait before checking in.

We saved a night’s accommodation. It cost us energy.

We arrived at night but couldn’t check in until later. We ended up in a park with our bags, tired and hungry. We wanted to try khinkali and khachapuri already, but first we had to make it to the start of the day.

If I did this trip again, I’d arrange somewhere to sleep after the night flight, even if it meant paying for the previous night. The savings took a noticeable toll on our first day.

Sometimes the first adventure in a new country is simply finding somewhere to sleep.

What mattered to us when choosing accommodation

We stayed in Tbilisi’s old town. When choosing a place, we considered reviews, the condition of the apartment, whether we could make a simple breakfast and how far it was from transport and excursion meeting points.

  • Read full reviews. Especially comments about hot water, cleanliness and noise at night.
  • Match the location to your plans. A beautiful neighbourhood doesn’t automatically make it convenient for excursions.
  • Think about everyday details. A kitchen and washing machine were more useful to us than a perfect interior photo.

The courtyard wasn’t luxurious, but it had atmosphere. Sometimes a place stays with you for something other than a polished picture.

The botanical garden: slowing down after the journey

Once we had rested, we made it to the botanical garden. There were trees, water, bamboo, a bridge and plenty of reasons to stop with the camera. After the hot city streets, it felt noticeably more pleasant to walk here.

[pair]

What I’d keep in the plan for another trip

A free first day. No packed list of sights and no expectation that we could do everything straight off the plane. First sleep, food and a walk near our accommodation. The adventures could come after that.

This is just the beginning of our trip. The episode covers our arrival, first walks, accommodation and an attempt to get to a karting track. Any prices and conditions in the video relate to our visit, so check them again before travelling.

georgia-excursions.title: What to check before booking an excursion in Georgia
georgia-excursions.description: My checklist after travelling in Georgia: reading reviews, working out the full cost and understanding how much time you’ll spend on the road.
georgia-excursions.label: Georgia / Tried it ourselves
georgia-excursions.alt: Vlad and Anya near Jvari with Mtskheta in the background
georgia-excursions.cardTitle: What to check before an excursion in Georgia
georgia-excursions.cardDescription: Three things I now check before booking: reviews, the full price and travel time.
georgia-excursions.body:
We took several excursions during our trip to Georgia. Some moments stayed with us for the views; others for the long journeys and costs that weren’t obvious from the advertised price. Now I check three things before booking.

1. Reviews: how many, and what do they actually say?

A rating alone tells you little about how a day will go. I look at how many people left it and read what they actually mention. Details about the pace, stops and transport are more useful to me than another “everything was great”.

A useful question is: what about this excursion might be inconvenient for us personally? That makes it easier to know which comments to look for.

2. The full cost, not just the headline price

On one of our excursions, the initial price didn’t include lunch, extra activities and some transfers. That isn’t necessarily a problem, as long as you know before setting off.

  • What is already included?
  • Which tickets or transfers cost extra?
  • Which activities can you skip?
  • How much will you need for the whole day, including food?

I’d save the itinerary and the organiser’s answers before paying. That makes it easier to revisit the details if you forget something.

Compare the whole day you’ll experience, rather than two starting prices.

3. How much time will you actually spend travelling?

Places can look close together on a map. But several hours on a bus through mountain roads is a different experience, especially if you get motion sickness. Some of our excursions took almost the entire day.

Now I ask about transfer times, when we’ll return and how much time we’ll have at the actual sights. I also avoid making important plans immediately afterwards.

[landscape]

A short checklist before booking

Read detailed reviews. Calculate the whole budget. Ask about time on the bus and at stops. Then decide whether that day suits your energy, interests and pace.

These are lessons from my own trip. Check the details of any particular excursion with its organiser: there is no universal itinerary or fixed price here.

kazbegi-paragliding.title: Paragliding in Kazbegi: I was afraid of heights, but went for it
kazbegi-paragliding.description: My tandem paragliding experience during an excursion to Kazbegi: nerves before take-off, powerful impressions and exhaustion after a packed day.
kazbegi-paragliding.label: Kazbegi / A first time
kazbegi-paragliding.cardTitle: Afraid of heights. Paragliding in Kazbegi anyway.
kazbegi-paragliding.cardDescription: Mountains, ten minutes of strong emotions and a very sleepy journey back.
kazbegi-paragliding.body:
I was afraid of heights. Then, during our trip to Georgia, an opportunity came up to go paragliding with an instructor. These are the moments you travel for, right? But knowing that and actually deciding to take off are two different things.

The nerves started before the flight

That day we were on an excursion towards Kazbegi. Mountains changed outside the window, with stops and new views along the way. The flight became the strongest impression of the day and the most unfamiliar experience for me.

I was scared before the start. Then the familiar sense of scale seemed to disappear: trees, roads and tiny cows below. It was hard to believe I was actually up above all of it.

After landing, I called it the best ten minutes of my life. That’s how intense those first emotions were.

The beautiful view is only half the story

I got very motion sick, especially on the descent. After landing, I wanted some time to recover. We decided to skip the next climb to Gergeti Church because I didn’t have the energy or desire to continue at that point.

That belongs in an honest account of the trip too. You can have an amazing time and still end up so tired that you just want a quiet rest of the day.

[sleep]

What stayed with me afterwards

The excursion took about ten hours. Anya and I slept on the way back, and that became part of the story as well. Not every day ends with an energetic speech to the camera.

I’m glad I went for it. But this is my personal experience, not a promise that someone else will feel the same.

Was it worth it for me?

Yes. For the view and for the feeling of doing something I had been afraid of. And the places we didn’t have energy for that day give us a reason to return.

car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.title: 10 hours filming and over 30 editing: making my car challenge video
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.description: Behind my most demanding episode: evenings developing the idea, a city-wide shoot with Lyokha and over 30 hours editing in DaVinci Resolve.
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.label: Behind the scenes / Filming and editing
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.alt: Vlad and Lyokha getting into a convertible for the first time during their car challenge
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.cardTitle: Making my most demanding video: filming and editing
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.cardDescription: Ten hours filming, over thirty editing and a car challenge I put a huge amount of work into.
car-challenge-behind-the-scenes.body:
This car challenge became the most demanding episode on my channel. Filming took about ten hours, and editing took more than thirty. But it started earlier, with several free evenings spent developing the idea.

A few evenings before the first shot

Before filming, I analysed the idea, looked for similar videos and worked on the rules. During my own search, I couldn’t find a YouTube video with the same format, so I decided to give it a try.

I wanted a car challenge that would also appeal to people who simply enjoy a good story. Before meeting Lyokha, I needed to work out what our game was and how to explain it to a viewer.

About ten hours around the city with Lyokha

We travelled all over the city while filming. The episode had a challenge at its centre, but the moments I remember most are the genuine reactions you can’t script beforehand.

[media:32]

One was getting into a convertible for the first time and both being blown away. Then came the speed, sound, wind and smiles. In moments like that, the emotions for the camera happen by themselves.

[media:33]

Over thirty hours in DaVinci Resolve

After filming came another big job: putting the episode together. Editing took over thirty hours. I used lots of effects I’d wanted to learn for a long time, and this video finally gave me a reason to try them.

[media:29]

My main focus was pace and viewer retention. I wanted the story to keep moving and stay interesting through to the end. The finished timeline is a useful reminder of how much work happens on the other side of the screen.

Behind the finished episode: about ten hours filming, over thirty editing and several evenings of preparation.

The work continued after the edit

I ran two A/B tests with different titles and thumbnails. I’ve written a separate story about those A/B tests, the options I compared and what the first report shows.

What the result meant to me

All my friends who watched the episode enjoyed it. They told me it was easy to watch in one sitting, including people who aren’t into cars. That feedback meant a lot: I wanted viewers to see the people and emotions behind the machines.

I take those comments as feedback from friends. It’s too early to judge retention across the whole audience from them. As the creator, though, I’m happy that people whose opinions matter to me felt the work I put into it.

[media:34]

At the end, Lyokha and I shake hands. After a long filming day and all the work that followed, that shot feels like a fitting end to a story I wanted to see through.

car-challenge-ab-tests.title: Two A/B tests for one video: choosing a title and thumbnail
car-challenge-ab-tests.description: The titles and thumbnails I tested for my car challenge: the first YouTube report, a second set of options and my two current favourite thumbnails.
car-challenge-ab-tests.label: Behind the scenes / Titles and thumbnails
car-challenge-ab-tests.alt: Car challenge thumbnail featuring Vlad, Lyokha and the Russian words for “Do it in 3 hours”
car-challenge-ab-tests.cardTitle: One video, two A/B tests: titles and thumbnails
car-challenge-ab-tests.cardDescription: The options I compared, the figures in the first report and the two thumbnails I currently like most.
car-challenge-ab-tests.body:
After about ten hours filming and more than thirty editing my car challenge, I wanted to give its title and thumbnail the same care. I ran two A/B tests with different combinations of titles and images.

There’s a separate story about filming and editing the episode. This one is about the different ways I tried presenting the same adventure to a new viewer.

The first test: three ways to describe the challenge

The first round compared three title-and-thumbnail combinations. One explained the task directly: find the most expensive car in three hours. Another led with “a licence or connections”. The third focused on the car we found in Minsk.

[media:27]
First A/B test: watch-time share shown in YouTube’s report
Title, translated from RussianShare
Find the most expensive car in the city in 3 hours29%
A licence or connections? Who will find a more expensive car in 3 hours?36.1%
The most expensive car we found in 3 hours in Minsk34.9%

The screenshot labels the metric as watch-time share. YouTube’s summary says that all variants performed well. That is how I’m recording the first test’s outcome.

The licence-or-connections option has the largest share in this report, at 36.1%. The report’s conclusion doesn’t single out a clear winner. I’m sharing one specific experiment from my own channel.

Round two: new title-and-image combinations

For the next test I prepared another set. The screenshot shows the options ready for comparison: a direct explanation of the challenge, the conflict between a licence and connections, and a question about who could get into cars with the greatest combined value in three hours.

[media:28]

I wanted to look at the same story through its rules, the rivalry between participants and the result. The second-round screenshot shows the setup; I’m leaving that round’s outcome open here for now.

My two current favourite thumbnails

These are the two I currently favour. The first combines a close-up reaction with a red car. The second shows Lyokha and me, the cars and the prominent three-hour limit.

[media:30] [media:31]

That is my current preference as the creator. I like how these images capture the mood and make it clear that a car adventure is waiting inside.

Why I kept these tests

I want to remember the whole journey of an episode, from the idea and the shoot to its first encounter with a new viewer. These screenshots record what I actually tried and what result I actually received.

You can watch the finished episode below and decide which title and thumbnail best represent its story.
